**Reproduced possible teaching shortcut.** Generator SHA-256
`513b681db0dfd9c530f867d70905b082bd14353d2d2c4b77484b2bbe529da7ea`,
executed rule hash `77504f6c55fa`.

Under the direct same-seed consecutive-index assembly, seed `2`, difficulty
`easy`, start index `11` gives five demonstrations with seed counts
`[1, 1, 2, 2, 2]` and a query with three seeds. The rival rule “expand at most
the first two seed rectangles; leave any additional seed unchanged” matches the
canonical Racket output on every demonstration and differs on the query. The
generator's declared `lesson_identifiable` hook returns no finding for this
window. All six inputs pass `self_check`; Racket output matches the task's Python
mirror on all six.

Exact grids, rectangle boxes, rival outputs, Racket outputs, hashes, and command
are in `checks/audit/1856980929fe/analysis.json` and
`checks/audit/1856980929fe/input.json`. This establishes a lawful generated
counterexample for that direct assembly. I did not measure how often the current
production assembler selects this exact start, so production prevalence is
unknown. No audit-target files were changed.
